text: The Inuit are peoples of the far north, living from Alaska across northern Canada to Greenland.
Their name, Inuit, means “the people” in their languages, Inuktitut and Kalaallisut.
src: Indigenous peoples of the Arctic and Subarctic, from the Bering Strait coast of Chukotka and northern Alaska across northern Canada to Greenland
Inuit is the word for “the people” in Inuktitut and in West Greenlandic (Kalaallisut)

text: Their ancestors, the Thule people, spread east from Alaska across the Arctic about 1,000 years ago.
They reached Greenland about 900 years ago and settled there.
src: The Thule people, ancestors of the Inuit, emerge from the Bering Strait and western Alaska and spread east across the Arctic
c. 1100 CE: Inuit migrants reach west Greenland and settle there

text: For centuries Inuit lived by hunting whales, seals, caribou and fish, and they shared food with the whole community.
They travelled by dog sled and by qajaq, a one-person sealskin boat that others copied as the kayak.
src: They lived by hunting whales, seals, caribou and other animals / shared food within the household and, to a large extent, the whole community / They hunted whales, above all the bowhead, seals, polar bears, muskoxen, caribou, birds and fish
The qajaq, a one-person sealskin boat that could be righted even when completely overturned, was copied by others as the kayak / travelling by qajaq, umiaq and dog sled

text: Inuit carved small animals and people from ivory and bone, and today they also make prints and stone sculptures.
In the old beliefs, every person, animal and thing had a spirit, so hunters showed respect to the animals.
src: Small carvings of animals and people in ivory and bone were followed in modern times by prints and stone sculpture
all things, humans included, had a form of spirit / a hunt that failed to show respect and the customary supplication would give the freed spirits cause for revenge

text: Diseases brought by outsiders killed many Inuit, and Canada moved some families from their homes against their will.
Inuit won rights to their lands, and today Inuktitut is an official language of Nunavut in Canada.
src: Diseases brought by whalers and explorers caused mass death / In the 1950s Canada began to settle Inuit in permanent villages, at times against their will / 17 families were taken from Inukjuak to Resolute and Grise Fiord
Inuit organised from the 1970s and won land claims, among them the agreement that created Nunavut in 1999 / Inuktitut is an official language of Nunavut
